lifecycle.decommission: The layout is a declared shape, not the data: decommission releases the layout record only after the Storage.Volume(s) realizing its entries are released by their consumers. Deleting the realizing volumes is the DATA-DESTRUCTIVE step and follows Storage.Volume's own decommission rules.

metadata.description: The declared DISK LAYOUT of a compute consumer (born from the 2026-07-29 Compute reconciliation: per-disk shape left Compute.VirtualMachine — one hand-authored source per concept). An ordered set of named entries — each a disk-shaped unit with a size, an optional storage class, an optional role, and an optional boot position — that a consumer (a VM's spec.layout_ref) realizes and consumable Storage.Volume records back. The entry `name` is the stable identity reconvergence joins on.

context.purpose: Declares the per-disk shape of a compute consumer — named, sized entries with boot designation — as its own record, so disk layout is authored once and referenced, never duplicated inside each consumer.
context.plain_description: The list of disks a machine should have: each entry names a disk (`name`, the stable join key), sizes it (`size`), and may pin a provider storage class (`storage_class`), state what the disk is for (`role`: boot/data/log), and place it in the boot order (`boot_order`). A VM points at one layout via its `layout_ref`; the consumable Storage.Volume records that realize each entry join back on the entry's name. The layout is shape, not data — the volumes carry the data.
use_when: You need a VM's (or other compute consumer's) disks declared as portable intent — sizes, roles, boot designation — separate from the consumer's own sizing.
You need reconvergence to join realized volumes back to declared disks by a stable per-entry identity.
You need one disk layout shared or compared across consumers instead of restated inline in each.
not_for: The consumable volume itself — Storage.Volume; a layout entry may be realized by one.
The provisioning policy — Platform.StorageClass; an entry references a class by name.
Host-local ZFS/LVM layout a host service mounts — Storage.Dataset / Storage.Pool.
The VM's numeric storage requirements (min_iops, encryption) — those live on the consumer's `storage` descriptor.
works_with: Compute.VirtualMachine — the consumer that realizes this layout (spec.layout_ref).
Storage.Volume — the consumable volume(s) realizing each entry (realized_by_volume).
Platform.StorageClass — the class an entry's storage_class names.

entries.description: The declared disks, in declaration order. Entry names MUST be unique within the layout — the name is the stable identity that reconvergence joins on (a realized volume binds to an entry by name, surviving reorder and resize).

name.description: Stable entry identity, unique within the layout — the join key reconvergence uses to bind a realized Storage.Volume back to this declared disk. Lowercase DNS-label shape.

size.description: Requested disk size, quantity form (e.g. 100Gi, 500GB) — the class-aligned size pattern shared with Compute memory sizing.

storage_class.description: Optional provider-advertised storage class reference (a Platform.StorageClass handle) this entry's realizing volume should be provisioned from. Authored by handle; deferred resolution supported.

role.description: Optional role of this disk, e.g. boot | data | log. Convention: the boot entry carries role `boot` (and, where order matters, boot_order 0); a layout declares at most one boot entry.

boot_order.description: Optional boot position (0 = first). Absent = provider default. Boot designation lives here — on the layout entry — not on the consumer.

realized_volumes.description: Per-entry realization map: for each entry name, the Storage.Volume (handle/uuid) realizing it — populated as volumes bind via the realized_by_volume relation. The binding surface a consumer reads to see which declared disk became which volume.

relationships.name: realized_by_volume
relationships.description: Each entry may be realized by a consumable Storage.Volume; the realizing volume joins on the entry's stable name.
